6.5.1
Modernization of the Use of the Town of Whitby Corporate Logo by Members of Council
Moved by Mayor Roy
Recommendation:
Whereas pursuant to Section 4 of the Municipal Act, 2001, the Town of Whitby is constituted as a municipal body corporate;
Whereas Sections 5 and 9 of the Municipal Act, 2001 establish the framework through which a municipality exercises its corporate powers, including its rights and privileges, through Council;
Whereas the Town of Whitby’s corporate logo, crest and associated branding are corporate identifiers and intellectual property interests that 
...
he policy expressly prohibit the use of the corporate logo for municipal election campaigns, political fundraising, partisan political advertising, personal commercial activities, or communications that falsely imply an official position or endorsement of Council;
Protection of Corporate Identity: That appropriate safeguards be established to protect the Town’s intellectual property, maintain brand consistency and clearly identify communications issued by individual Members of Council rather than by the Corporation;
Streamlined Administration: That staff develop standardized branding guidelines and approved logo formats that allow Members of Council to undertake routine municipal communications without requiring individual approval for each use, provided the communications comply with the policy;
Legal and Policy Compliance: That the proposed amendments be reviewed for consistency with the Municipal Act, 2001, the Municipal Elections Act, 1996, applicable copyright and trademark legislation, the Council Code of Conduct, the Use of Corporate Resources for Election Purposes Policy G 070, and other relevant Town policies; and,
Implementation: That staff report back to Council with recommended policy amendments, any required authorizing by-law or amendments to existing by-laws, and an implementation framework for Council’s consideration.
